title: "In a formula, x^2 is not the square of x"
ref: STA-01
categories: [Statistics and models]

extrait: 'length(coef(lm(dist ~ speed + speed^2, data = cars)))'
reponse: '2'
attendu: "three coefficients: the intercept, speed and speed squared"

::: {.piege}
```{r}
fit <- lm(dist ~ speed + speed^2, data = cars)
coef(fit)
```
:::

## Why

In a formula, operators describe the terms of the model, not arithmetic. `+` adds a term, `-` removes one, `:` is an interaction, and `^` crosses terms up to a degree: `(a + b)^2` means `a + b + a:b`. `speed^2` is therefore the interaction of `speed` with itself, that is `speed`, and the model has no squared term.

R accepts the formula without a message, and the model fits: it is simply a straight line. The same reading applies to `y ~ x - 1`, which removes the intercept instead of subtracting 1.

## The remedy

Protect arithmetic with `I()`, as `?formula` suggests, or use `poly()` for a polynomial.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
fit <- lm(dist ~ speed + I(speed^2), data = cars)
coef(fit)
```
:::
